page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8y.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the arm64 architecture, running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 32-core Alibaba Yitian YiTian710 processor operating at 2.75 GHz with a 1:1 mapping of virtual CPUs to physical cores without simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 64 MB of shared L3 cache. The instance is paired with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. It incorporates hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions, does not include local storage, and includes no discrete graphics processors. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the processor in the middle 50% for standard computational loads, scoring 1815.99 on single-core stress-ng and 57653.7 on multi-core stress-ng. PassMark tests confirm this mid-range CPU performance with a score of 22713.48, an encryption score of 5242.62, and a physics score of 4975.66. In contrast, the memory subsystem and specific multi-threaded throughput tests demonstrate stronger relative performance, ranking in the top 25%. This is evidenced by a PassMark memory score of 2907.18, PassMark database operations at 23774.36, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 272.21 GB/sec. Large uncached memory bandwidth reaches 97.81 GB/sec read and 47.9 GB/sec write.

Application benchmarks show consistent mid-tier execution across operational scenarios. The instance delivers 50.18 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and maintains static web serving throughput of 34.16 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning workloads evaluated via small (135M) language models, it processes prompts at 1157.93 tokens per second and generates text at 178.64 tokens per second. Performance scales down predictably for medium (7B) language models, yielding 41.74 prompt tokens per second and 14.93 text generation tokens per second.

Because the server features a dedicated physical core per vCPU, it avoids resource contention typical of hyperthreaded architectures while delivering robust memory and database execution. However, relying strictly on remote storage volumes and lacking x86 vector extensions (AVX/AMX) means workloads must be arm64-compatible and not bounded by direct-attached NVMe requirements. The hardware profile is best matched for enterprise database operations, caching tiers, multi-threaded data decompression, backend application servers, and microservice infrastructure.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8y.8xlarge is a general-purpose arm64 server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by Alibaba's 32-core Yitian YiTian710 processor clocked at 2.75 GHz with dedicated physical cores, it supplies 128.0 GB of memory across a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, 16 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, and hardware AES encryption. The instance lacks local storage disks and discrete GPUs. In synthetic evaluations, the ecs.g8y.8xlarge posts average scores in stress-ng compute tests and general PassMark metrics, but ranks in the top 25% for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, PassMark memory performance, and database operations. Real-world tasks show 50.18 million Redis SET operations per second and 34.16 GB/sec static web throughput. Without hyperthreading or x86 instruction sets, it provides predictable throughput for database systems, memory-centric caching tiers, web services, and arm64-native containerized applications.
